newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil casts doubt on released results.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil casts doubt on released results.

text.p: A spokesman for Russia's largest oil company, LUKoil, said on Wednesday that he could not completely confirm net profit and sales figures for 1996 announced by LUKoil president Vagit Alekperov on Tuesday.

"We will publish an official statement in the second half of the day," the spokesman said. "The figures given yesterday by Alekperov were correct but do not reflect the real situation of the company's affairs."
Alekperov told businessmen in Moldova on Tuesday LUKoil's net profit was 1.30 trillion roubles in 1996 on sales of 35 trillion.
In 1995, LUKoil had a net profit of 2.40 trillion on sales of 29.57 trillion.

But last month LUKoil said net profit in the first nine months of 1996 was 2.609 trillion roubles, up from 1.197 trillion in the same 1995 period, and sales were 33 trillion in the nine months after 13.75 trillion over that period in 1995.
LUKoil, one of a dozen integrated oil companies formed after the break-up of the Soviet Union, is one of Russia's most open and investor-oriented firms.
Its shares make up about a third of Russian stock market capitalisation by some equities analysts' estimates.
Many Russian companies still issue confusing or imprecise information and Russian accounting standards make it difficult for investors to interpret Russian company figures.
